tests.name: doc self-check (Level 1)
keys and fields are independent
delete then set again
delete of a missing key or field returns False and changes nothing
delete removes only that field
same field name under different keys
a key emptied by deletes is missing, then can be recreated
repeated overwrites keep a single field
key and field names do not collide
interleaved operations across keys
random records
doc self-check (Level 2)
sorted by field name, not insertion order or value
scans reflect overwrites and deletes
an empty prefix matches every field
prefix equal to a whole field name, or longer than every name
prefix match is not a substring or suffix match
scans of a key whose fields were all deleted
scan shows only the requested key
string order puts a prefix before its extensions
scans after delete, re-add and overwrite
a single field has no separators and values print as-is
random records and scans
doc self-check (Level 3)
a TTL field disappears from get and scans
set_with_ttl on an existing field replaces value and TTL
expiry boundary in scans and get
delete just before expiry succeeds, at expiry fails
a plain set clears a TTL before it expires
set_with_ttl replaces the TTL, shorter or longer
an expired field can be set again with a fresh lifetime
a key whose fields all expired is missing
a ttl of 1 has expired by the next call
fields expire independently inside scans
a plain set on a sibling field leaves the TTL alone
random records with TTLs
doc self-check (Level 4)
backup and restore round trip
a restored TTL keeps its remaining lifetime
restore picks the latest backup at or before the target
restoring one backup twice measures lifetime from each restore
fields without a TTL never expire after a late restore
backup counts only keys with a live field
a field expiring exactly at backup time is not saved
writes after a backup or a restore do not change the backup
restore replaces the whole database and keeps every backup
set and set_with_ttl after a restore replace the restored TTL
an empty backup restores an empty database
remaining lifetime comes from the chosen backup
random sequence with backups and restores
